messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Polish, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Polish line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase (Polish) | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|-----------------------|------------------------------|------------------------|--------| | Ond' | causal conjunction introducing a reason | Dlatego | therefore / thus | OK | | io | 1st‑person singular pronoun (subject) | — (subject omitted) | — | UNNECESSARY | | per | preposition marking benefit/purpose | za | for | OK | | lo | definite article (the) | — (article omitted) | — | UNNECESSARY | | tuo | 2nd‑person possessive adjective | twoje | your | OK | | me' | abstract noun “best”, i.e. the addressee’s good | dobro | good / benefit | OK | | penso | 1st‑sg present verb “think” | myślę | I think | OK | | e | coordinating conjunction “and” | i | and | OK | | discerno | 1st‑sg present verb “deem, judge” | uznaję | I deem | OK | | che | subordinating conjunction “that” | że | that | OK | | tu | 2nd‑sg pronoun (subject) | — (subject omitted) | — | UNNECESSARY | | mi | 1st‑sg pronoun (object) | mną | me | OK | | segui | 2nd‑sg present verb “follow” | podążysz | you will follow | OK | | e | coordinating conjunction “and” | i | and | OK | | io | 1st‑sg pronoun (subject) | — (subject omitted) | — | UNNECESSARY | | sarò | 1st‑sg future “will be” | będę | I will be | OK | | tua | 2nd‑sg possessive adjective | twoim | your | OK | | guida | feminine noun “guide” | przewodnikiem | guide (instrumental) | OK | | e | coordinating conjunction “and” | i | and | OK | | trarrotti | 2nd‑sg future “will lead you” | poprowadzę cię | I will lead you | OK | | di | preposition “from” (part of *di qui*) | stąd | from here / hence | OK | | qui | adverb “here” (part of *di qui*) | stąd | from here | OK | | per | preposition “to/through” (introducing destination) | do | to / into | OK | | loco | masculine noun “place” | miejsca | place (genitive) | OK | | etterno | masculine adjective “eternal” | wiecznego | eternal (genitive) | OK |

### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: `io` (twice), `lo`, `tu`, `io` (third occurrence) – Polish drops subject pronouns and definite articles, so they are naturally omitted. - No **MISSING**, **WRONG**, or **GRAMMAR** errors were detected; all retained elements agree in gender, number, and case.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Polish script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Polish text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
